incident-bot: PagerDuty: Rate limiter error spike for /v1/generate - 429s observed across multiple clusters. Alert severity: P2. Docs: https://runbook.internal/rate-limiter

pagerduty: New incident assigned to Priya (oncall). Incident key: PD-87821. Auto-escalation in 10m if unacked.

Priya (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Quick summary?

Alex (eng-sre): seeing a surge of 429s and some 503s from limiter-proxy. Metrics: 95th latency up 5x, error rate 18% for token service. Likely quota mapper misapplied to a subset of tenants after the rollout at 04:12 UTC.

Maya (eng-runtime): Confirmed. I pulled linker logs. We got a spike of malformed quota keys from the mapper service causing it to return deny responses. Example log:

```
2024-05-10T04:12:05Z quota-mapper ERROR tenant=acme123 key=unset action=deny reason="quota_key_missing"
2024-05-10T04:12:06Z limiter-proxy WARN tenant=acme123 status=429 route=/v1/generate pref_hit=false
```
Maya (eng-runtime): The rollout included a change that normalizes tenant metadata into a new header X-Tenant-Hash. Some upstream clients still send the old header, resulting in mapper returning default deny for those keys. That matches the pattern: a subset of tenants, mostly older SDK versions, are impacted.

Priya (oncall): Customer impact? Any big customers in that subset?

Alex (eng-sre): Early list shows 3 mid-market customers showing elevated 429s (acme123, beta-inc, quickly). No GA enterprise customers yet, but some paid pipelines saw retries. Estimated failed requests ~12k in 15m window.

Sam (prod-eng): Paging cadence: do we want to roll back the mapper change or apply a fast mitigation (allowlist fallback)? Rollback will touch CI and could take ~25m. Fallback change could be a single config flip on mapper (tolerate old header) and be <5m.

Maya (eng-runtime): I can flip tolerant mode. It adds a compatibility check: if X-Tenant-Hash missing, fall back to legacy-header parsing. I have a one-line config: `compat_mode: legacy_header_fallback = true`.

Priya (oncall): Do it. Also open a PD note for customers impacted. Alex, can you confirm rate limits won't be abused if we relax the mapper?

Alex (eng-sre): We will still enforce quotas at limiter with tenant_id after mapping; fallback only affects mapping path. Rate limit counters are unchanged. Risk low. Proceed.

Maya (eng-runtime): executing now. Command: `kubectl -n runtime patch configmap quota-mapper -p '{"data":{"compat_mode":"legacy_header_fallback=true"}}' && kubectl rollout restart deploy/quota-mapper`

Maya (eng-runtime): done. Rollout started, pods terminating then starting. Watch: `kubectl get pods -l app=quota-mapper -w`

Alex (eng-sre): Observing traffic. 2 mins after rollout start: error rate trending down from 18% -> 6%. 429s for previously affected tenants dropping.

Priya (oncall): Noted. PD update: "Mitigation applied: quota-mapper compatibility mode enabled. Impacted customers: acme123, beta-inc, quickly. Monitoring for 30m. Next update in 10m or on change."

pagerduty: Auto-escalation cancelled by ack.

Maya (eng-runtime): Rollout complete on all 3 replicas. No crashloops.

Sam (prod-eng): Can we run a synthetic against those tenants to validate?

Alex (eng-sre): Running curl loop against acme123 env with legacy header. Script: 
```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -H 'X-Legacy-Tenant: acme123' -H 'Authorization: Bearer test' https://api.redwood/run/v1/generate | jq -r '.status' ; sleep 0.2; done
```
Alex (eng-sre): Results: responses now 200/50. Previously was ~60% 429. Good.

Priya (oncall): Great. Next: postmortem action items?

Maya (eng-runtime): Short term: revert compatibility off once we ship a more robust adapter; add a canary that validates presence of X-Tenant-Hash in clients. Long term: add backward-compatible header translation at ingress so mapper never sees old headers.

Alex (eng-sre): Also add an alert that triggers when a particular tenant's 429 rate increases > 5% relative to baseline. Current alert grouped by service masked this pattern.

Priya (oncall): Assigning actions: Maya -> implement ingress translation ticket (#TKT-4567). Alex -> new tenant-specific 429 anomaly alert (#TKT-4568). Sam -> coordinate SDK release notes to customers and check client versions in use (#TKT-4569). I'll create the PD incident with these items.

Priya (oncall): On-call handoff: Sam is taking over for the next 3 hours to monitor post-mitigation. Priya handing off at 04:40 UTC.

Sam (prod-eng): Ack. I'll watch latency, 429s, and limit counters. If error rate rises >3% I'll escalate back to eng-sre.

Maya (eng-runtime): Leaving logs & patch diff in the incident doc: https://runbook.internal/incidents/1729991234

Alex (eng-sre): Customers notified via PD notes and support ticket #SUP-98912.

Priya (oncall): Closing PD alert to notify stakeholders, keeping this thread for postmortem. Thanks all :thumbsup:

pagerduty: Incident marked resolved by Priya (oncall).

Sam (prod-eng): Follow-up: we should schedule a short postmortem meeting tomorrow. I'll ping calendar.

Maya (eng-runtime): Will draft timeline and include log snippets and the patch diff.

Alex (eng-sre): Add a regression test in deploy pipeline to reject mapper changes that remove legacy handling without a migration plan.

Priya (oncall): Last check: 30m window looks stable. I'll update the incident status to 'mitigated' and move to postmortem. Thread closed unless someone reopens.

Maya (eng-runtime): noted.

Alex (eng-sre): thanks everyone.
